title: How Do Habits Form?
paragraphs: Habits are things we do often, usually without thinking about them. Brushing your teeth, drinking coffee in the morning or checking your phone are all habits.
Scientists say that many habits have three parts. First, something reminds us to act. Next, we do the action. Finally, we get a reward, something that feels good.
When we repeat this many times, the brain learns it. After a while, the reminder is enough, and we start the action automatically.
To start a new habit, it helps to begin with something small and do it at the same time or place every day. In one study, people needed about two months, on average, to make a new habit automatic.
